lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: product or service idea

objective: Learners compare invented start-up costs across pretend venture ideas and test a scaled production plan against a simulated budget.
scenario: Ottilie is a made-up fifth grader choosing among three pretend venture ideas with invented start-up costs of $85.00 for a print series, $120.50 for a garden kit, and $64.75 for a card set. Her simulated budget is $300.00.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Look across Ottilie's three invented start-up costs.

prompts.text: What is the lowest start-up cost among the three ideas?

tasks.directions: Find the spread between Ottilie's dearest and cheapest ideas, then compare two of them directly.

prompts.text: How much more is the dearest start-up than the cheapest?
Between the print series and the garden kit, which costs less to start?

tasks.directions: Ottilie chooses the card set and plans 4 production batches, each costing the same start-up amount.

prompts.text: How much of the $300.00 budget remains?

tasks.directions: The cheapest start was not automatically the strongest plan.

prompts.text: What evidence about buyers would Ottilie need before four batches of the cheapest idea beats one batch of a dearer one?

remediation: When a learner selects on cost alone, have them write who buys each of Ottilie's three products and why, before any comparison is drawn.
extension: Ask the learner how many garden kits Ottilie could start inside $300.00 and what that implies for her choice.
